title: Beyond the Last Stone
description: Read for a concrete way to distinguish what people know, claim, and choose.

readerInvitation.reasonToExist: Beyond the Last Stone makes careful thinking a matter of staying alive. Hungry people must compare observations, inherited stories, and reasons for acting together.
readerInvitation.readerPromise: Read for a concrete way to distinguish what people know, claim, and choose.
readerInvitation.audienceFit: This book suits readers who enjoy philosophical fiction with direct, spare language.
readerInvitation.closingInvitation: Begin with Fire After the Herd, then follow those questions into the city.
readerOutcomes: Read for a concrete way to distinguish what people know, claim, and choose.

contentSamples.readingValue: Reading their disagreements reveals why useful stories still require attention to their purpose.
It gives readers distinctions to test, rather than conclusions delivered by an outside lecturer.

reservedForReading: Later plot revelations, deaths, reversals and final resolutions
Exhaustive retelling and unsupported claims about real technology

scenes.title: The missing herd
scenes.intent: The herd has not returned, and a convincing story will not feed the camp.
scenes.knownBefore: A prospective reader is choosing a book.
scenes.knownAfter: Beyond the Last Stone begins with a prehistoric community facing hunger and an uncertain route forward.

objects.meaning: The low river reaches the black rock, which sits in it like the back of a sleeping animal.
An empty trail runs up into the pass; no animal or fresh hoof sign is on it.
Flat ridges frame an empty pass on the right where the herd should appear.
A small fire: the camp’s only warmth while the herd is late.
The remaining food, small enough to sit on one hide.
Kee, the oldest member, who remembers rivers, herds and names.
Karr, the storyteller who keeps what stories can carry.
Ar, a young hunter who asks what people have actually seen.

objects.meaning: One route climbs toward the high ground and passes behind the ridge.

A second route leaves along the low ground.
A patch of old snow where signs can be inspected.
Three large bear prints with claw marks: something that was seen, not where the bear is now.
A remembered herd drawn like an ochre cave painting on story-smoke rising from Karr’s raised hand: what stories carry, not animals present today.
Taan, Ar’s companion who carries spears and first names the bear.

scenes.title: Thought beside the fire
scenes.intent: Through tracks, counting stones, and fireside arguments, the novel makes early ideas about knowledge feel immediate.
scenes.knownBefore: They must decide together before anyone can be sure which signs to trust.
scenes.knownAfter: Its people need knowledge, but they also need courage, shared memory, and one another.

scenes.title: Join the River People
scenes.intent: The adventure is discovering how an idea can guide a life without becoming a certainty.
scenes.knownBefore: Its people need knowledge, but they also need courage, shared memory, and one another.
scenes.knownAfter: Join the River People at the first hungry camp, where every claim has somewhere to lead.

objects.meaning: A path from the camp ground toward the gap in the ridge; where it leads is left to the reader.
Low ridges beyond the first camp, continuing behind the book, with a gap the path leads into.
The fire of the first hungry camp.
A hide carrying a charcoal route line, part of it wiped away: guidance without a guarantee.
Beyond the Last Stone itself, with a small cairn on its cover: the invitation to read on from the first camp.
A bookmark at the opening chapter, Fire After the Herd.
Kee, the oldest member, who remembers rivers, herds and names.
Karr, the storyteller who keeps what stories can carry.
Ar, a young hunter who asks what people have actually seen.
Ar’s right arm bent, his hand at his chin: thinking along the path.
Ar’s right arm lowered again as he turns back to the camp.
